title: What to Know Before Switching to Whole House Heat Pumps | Ask This Old House
summary: This Old House walks through deciding whether to replace a gas furnace with a heat pump: climate zone, current fuel, system type, duct size and leakage.

verdicts.note: Median bill savings of $300-$650/yr for electric, oil and propane homes with AC compare with -$70 to $380/yr for gas homes with AC.
Counting capital cost, resistance and propane homes usually gain, but oil-heated homes usually take a private loss (65% are in cold climates), so oil is not among the best cases.
Edwards finds the primary heating fuel is a key driver: bill savings are highest where homes now heat with electricity or fuels other than gas.
RMI concludes that electrification has the greatest immediate cost and carbon benefit for oil and propane customers.
LBNL: the large energy cost reductions in electrification projects were most likely in homes with high pre-retrofit bills, such as those heating with propane or fuel oil.

Savings were highest against electric resistance, and the evaluators recommend targeting resistance-heated and propane-heated homes (always cheaper there) and, with caveats, oil homes; against gas there were essentially no running-cost savings.

UK households that previously used electric heating saw electricity use fall after a heat pump, while gas-boiler households paid slightly more to run one, which fits the claim for resistance heat; oil and propane are not analysed.
